newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS VOLATILE WEEK EASIER ON UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS VOLATILE WEEK EASIER ON UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar, dogged by heavy import pressure during the last two weeks, closed on Friday softer against hard currencies though dealers expected a reprieve on Monday in the form of a sizeable amount of export inflows.
"The market was very active today with the dollar keeping to its current high ranges," one dealer said.

"But (exchange) rates should come down next week because we're expecting U.S.$26 million to come into the market. That's quite a bit of money unless there are payments of a similar amount to be made," he added.

Dealers said heavy demand for foreign currency, mostly for loan repayments, had pushed the dollar down by three percent within the last two weeks. They added that such a fall would normally be spread over three months.
Dealers maintained however that there was no link between the depreciation and an on-going wrangle between government and civils servants over wage increases.

At the end of Friday's interbank session, the Zimbabwe dollar was trading weaker on the U.S. unit at 10.2500/3000 from Thursday's 10.1800/2500 while against sterling it dropped to 15.9640/16.0500 from 15.8400/9550.
It was also weaker at 6.9110/9470 versus the mark compared to 6.8830/9310 and was at 2.2850/2980 from 2.2560/2730 against South Africa's rand.
